tr: „No fire, only smoke.“ — komşu duman gördü.
en: „No fire, only smoke.“ — the neighbour saw the smoke.

tr: Mutfakta bir gün. Aynı anda kaç iş sürüyor?
en: A day in the kitchen. How many things are going on at once?

tr: „First“, „then“ ve „one day“ sırayı açıkça veriyor.
en: „First“, „then“ and „one day“ state the order openly.

tr: „At nine I was sleeping!“ — sekizde yemek pişiriyordu.
en: „At nine I was sleeping!“ — at eight she was cooking.

tr: „I used to play football, but I didn't use to like it.“
en: „I used to play football, but I didn't use to like it.“

tr: „I have never been abroad.“ — yurt dışına giden kardeşi.
en: „I have never been abroad.“ — the one going abroad is her brother.

tr: Düzensiz geçmişi yaz. Sonunda kayıp eşya formunu doldur.
en: Write the irregular past. At the end, fill in the lost property form.

tr: İki geçmişi bir arada yaz: süren iş ve onun içindeki an.
en: Write both pasts together: the action that was going on and the moment inside it.

tr: Önce baba, sonra anne, sonra kendisi, en son kız kardeşi.
en: First the father, then the mother, then herself, last her sister.

tr: Bir bilgisayar hikâyesi. Zaman ifadelerini sırayla yakala.
en: A story about a computer. Catch the time expressions in order.

tr: Bir çocukluk anlatısı. Eskiden ne vardı, sonra ne değişti?
en: A childhood story. What was there before, and what changed after that?

tr: İki sözcüğün farkı anlatılıyor. Kim hâlâ orada, kim döndü?
en: The difference between two words is explained. Who is still there, who came back?

tr: „In the bin. We ate bread and cheese.“ — pirinç çöpe gitti.
en: „In the bin. We ate bread and cheese.“ — the rice ended up in the bin.

tr: Geçmiş hakkında sorular. Her soru başka bir şeyi öğreniyor.
en: Questions about the past. Each question finds out something else.

tr: „Two weeks ago, I think.“ — „ago“ hep geçmişe doğru sayıyor.
en: „Two weeks ago, I think.“ — „ago“ always counts back into the past.

tr: Bir kazayı anlat ve geçmişi sor. Sonunda kaza formunu doldur.
en: Tell about an accident and ask about the past. At the end, fill in the accident form.

tr: „But my neighbour heard me and she came fast.“ — Ali yalnızdı.
en: „But my neighbour heard me and she came fast.“ — Ali was alone.

tr: Uzun bir günün anlatısı. Sıralama sözcükleri hikâyeyi taşıyor.
en: The story of a long day. The sequencing words carry the story.

tr: „I have been to Italy twice.“ — „been“ gidip döndüğünü söylüyor.
en: „I have been to Italy twice.“ — „been“ says he went and came back.

tr: Küçük bir kaza anlatılıyor. Ne oldu, ne kadar ciddi, sonrası ne?
en: A small accident is told. What happened, how serious, and what comes after?

tr: „Because my father was the coach!“ — sevmediğini iki kez söylüyor.
en: „Because my father was the coach!“ — he says twice that he did not like it.

tr: „First I got up at six.“ — otobüs ikinci, kitap bekleme sırasında.
en: „First I got up at six.“ — the bus comes second, the book while waiting.

tr: „I have moved four times in my life.“ — deneyim anlatan bir kalıp.
en: „I have moved four times in my life.“ — a pattern that reports experience.

tr: Bir tatil anlat. Sıralama sözcükleri cümleleri birbirine bağlıyor.
en: Tell about a holiday. The sequencing words tie the sentences together.

tr: Eski alışkanlıklar konuşuluyor. „used to“nun üç biçimi de geçiyor.
en: Old habits are the subject. All three forms of „used to“ turn up.

tr: Eski alışkanlıkları yaz. Olumluda „used“, olumsuz ve soruda „use“.
en: Write old habits. „used“ in the positive, „use“ in the negative and in questions.

tr: „Where did you go last month?“ — „did“ varken fiil ilk hâlinde: go.
en: „Where did you go last month?“ — with „did“ the verb stays in its base form: go.

tr: „But at the same time the sun was shining…“ — üç iş birlikte sürüyor.
en: „But at the same time the sun was shining…“ — three actions are going on together.

tr: „My sister has visited six countries.“ — iki, annenin Almanya sayısı.
en: „My sister has visited six countries.“ — two is the number of the mother's trips to Germany.

tr: „We stayed at a small hotel for five days.“ — iki saat uçağın rötarı.
en: „We stayed at a small hotel for five days.“ — two hours was the delay of the plane.

tr: „Last week I lost all my work on it.“ — iki gün önce bilgisayarı aldı.
en: „Last week I lost all my work on it.“ — two days ago he bought the computer.

tr: „My sister used to play with her doll…“ — futbol ve kütüphane yazarın.
en: „My sister used to play with her doll…“ — the football and the library are the writer's.

tr: „Yes, when I was a child. I used to play every day.“ — futbol Mert'in.
en: „Yes, when I was a child. I used to play every day.“ — the football was Mert's.

tr: Kaybolan bir telefonun hikâyesi. Ne zaman ne oldu, sırasıyla takip et.
en: The story of a lost phone. Follow in order what happened when.

tr: „At eight? I was cooking.“ — dokuzda uyuyordu, sabah otobüs bekliyordu.
en: „At eight? I was cooking.“ — at nine she was sleeping, in the morning waiting for the bus.

tr: „Because my friend was working. He came on Thursday.“ — başta yalnızdı.
en: „Because my friend was working. He came on Thursday.“ — at the beginning he was alone.

tr: „I used to play every day.“ — olumluda „used“, olumsuz ve soruda „use“.
en: „I used to play every day.“ — „used“ in the positive, „use“ in the negative and in questions.

tr: „I was waiting for the bus in the rain.“ — sürmekte olan iş, arka plan.
en: „I was waiting for the bus in the rain.“ — the action going on, the background.

tr: „At first I didn't like it.“ — „at first“ sonradan değiştiğini söylüyor.
en: „At first I didn't like it.“ — „at first“ says it changed later.

tr: „Ninety-two! And he was still working.“ — Ela yetmiş diye tahmin ediyor.
en: „Ninety-two! And he was still working.“ — Ela guesses seventy.

tr: „I bought a small bag for the phone.“ — telefonu bulundu, yenisini almadı.
en: „I bought a small bag for the phone.“ — the phone was found, he bought no new one.

tr: „My father has gone to Germany — he is away this week.“ — yani hâlâ orada.
en: „My father has gone to Germany — he is away this week.“ — so he is still there.

tr: „While I was working, it was raining all day.“ — iki iş aynı anda sürüyor.
en: „While I was working, it was raining all day.“ — two actions going on at the same time.

tr: „No, I haven't. But I want to go.“ — kısa cevap yardımcı fiili tekrarlıyor.
en: „No, I haven't. But I want to go.“ — the short answer repeats the auxiliary.

tr: „Only three days. After that I stayed with a friend.“ — on gün bütün tatil.
en: „Only three days. After that I stayed with a friend.“ — ten days was the whole trip.

tr: Anlatım sırası olayların sırası değil: en yeni olay ilk cümlede söyleniyor.
en: The order of the telling is not the order of the events: the newest one is in the first sentence.

tr: Deneyim sor ve anlat. Son görev „been“ ile „gone“ arasındaki farkı ölçüyor.
en: Ask about experience and tell about it. The last task measures the difference between „been“ and „gone“.

tr: „Last week I lost my phone on the bus.“ — istasyon telefonu geri aldığı yer.
en: „Last week I lost my phone on the bus.“ — the station is where he got it back.

tr: İki kişi dün ne yaptıklarını konuşuyor. Hangi iş sürüyordu, hangisi bir andı?
en: Two people talk about yesterday. Which action was going on, which was a single moment?

tr: „I fell on the stairs yesterday and I hurt my arm.“ — doktor „no break“ diyor.
en: „I fell on the stairs yesterday and I hurt my arm.“ — the doctor says „no break“.

tr: „Somebody brought a phone yesterday,“ she said. — kadın yalnız haberi veriyor.
en: „Somebody brought a phone yesterday,“ she said. — the woman only passes on the news.

tr: Deneyimler konuşuluyor. Dikkat: „has gone“ hâlâ orada, „has been“ döndü demek.
en: Experiences are the subject. Careful: „has gone“ means still there, „has been“ means back again.

tr: Önce soru, sonra cevap, sonra karşı taraf kendini anlatıyor, en son yeni soru.
en: First the question, then the answer, then the other side tells about herself, last a new question.

tr: Dört sıralama sözcüğü dört adımı işaretliyor: first, then, after that, finally.
en: Four sequencing words mark four steps: first, then, after that, finally.

tr: En eski olay iki hafta önce, en yenisi bu sabah. Zaman ifadeleri sırayı veriyor.
en: The oldest event was two weeks ago, the newest this morning. The time expressions give the order.

tr: „my brother has gone to London — he is away this week“ — „gone“ hâlâ orada demek.
en: „my brother has gone to London — he is away this week“ — „gone“ means he is still there.

tr: „While I was cooking, the phone rang…“ — „while“ süren işi, geçmiş zaman anı taşıyor.
en: „While I was cooking, the phone rang…“ — „while“ carries the action, the past tense the moment.

tr: Bir tatil anlatısı. Sıralama sözcüklerini takip et: first, then, after that, finally.
en: A holiday story. Follow the sequencing words: first, then, after that, finally.

tr: „I grew up in a small village near the sea.“ — ilkokul yan kasabada, şehir sonra geliyor.
en: „I grew up in a small village near the sea.“ — the primary school was in the next town, the city came later.

tr: „While I was cooking, the phone rang and I answered.“ — pişirmek arka plan, telefon bir an.
en: „While I was cooking, the phone rang and I answered.“ — the cooking is the background, the phone a moment.
